akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ﴾: its singular is "العِهْنَة", like "الصُوف" and "الصُّوفَة" (wool, a tuft of wool). As for His words ﴿مَا هِيَهْ﴾ with the hāʾ, it is because the pause on it is made with the hāʾ, since it is the end of a verse.

daas-irab:10-10.t: Like the i'rab of verse 3, and the hāʾ is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿نارٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حامِيَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is explicative (mufassira).

daas-irab:5-5.t: Conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle (ḥarf istiʾnāf); ﴿أما﴾ is a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), because the relative noun resembles the conditional; ﴿هو﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿راضِيَةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ مَن.

daas-irab:8-8.t: Conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ مَن.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿الْقارِعَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مَا الْقارِعَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of القارعة, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مَا الْقارِعَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَكُونُ النَّاسُ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun; ﴿كَالْفَراشِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of yakūn; ﴿الْمَبْثُوثِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الفراش; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ﴾.
He means: like a swarm of locusts climbing over one another; likewise people on that Day will surge into one another.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "كالصوف المنفوش" (like carded wool). It has been mentioned that the forms of the mountains are moved across the earth while, in the shape of mountains, they are like fine dust.
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ﴾.
Because their colours differ, like the colours of dyed wool (العهن).

farraa:6-6.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾.
[That is,] and his weight (وزنه). The Arabs say: هل لك فى درهم بميزان درهمك ووزن درهمك (Would you like a dirham of the weight of your dirham?), and they say: دارى بميزان دارك ووزن دارك (my house is the equal [lit. the balance/weight] of your house). The poet said:
قد كنتُ قبلَ لقائِكم ذا مِرَّةٍ * عندى لكلٍ مخاصم ميزانه
(Before meeting you I was a man of strength: I had, for every disputant, his match [lit. his balance].)
He means: I had [what matched] the weight of his speech and [could] refute it.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ﴾.
It has become his abode, as a woman gives shelter to her son; so, since he has no abode other than it, He made it a mother to him.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qāriʿa
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿القارِعَةُ﴾ ﴿ما القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 2] ("the Striking Calamity; what is the Striking Calamity?"): ”اَلْقارِعَةُ“, ”اَلْواقِعَةُ“ and ”اَلْحاقَّةُ“ are among the attributes of the Hour of Resurrection. ”اَلْقارِعَةُ“ is the one that strikes with terrors. We have already explained the iʿrāb of ﴿الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 1] ﴿ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 2], and like it is ﴿القارِعَةُ﴾ ﴿ما القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 2].

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النّاسُ كالفَراشِ المَبْثُوثِ﴾ ("the Day when people will be like scattered moths"): ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb (ẓarf); the meaning is: "it will be on the Day when people are like scattered moths". ”اَلْفَراشُ“ is what you see like small gnats, falling headlong into a fire. He likened people at the time of the Resurrection to spreading locusts and to scattered moths, because when they are resurrected they surge into one another, like locusts that surge into one another.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿كالعِهْنِ المَنفُوشِ﴾ ("like carded wool"): ”اَلْعِهْنُ“ is wool; its unit noun is ”عِهْنَةٌ“. One says ”عِهْنَةٌ“ and ”عِهْنٌ“, like ”صُوفَةٌ“ and ”صُوفٌ“.

zajjaj:6-7.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأمّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾ ﴿فَهُوَ في عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ﴾ ("as for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasing life"): [rāḍiya means] possessed of pleasure. Its meaning is: whose scales are heavy with good deeds, as you say ”لِفُلانٍ عِنْدِي وزْنٌ ثَقِيلٌ“ ("so-and-so has heavy weight with me"), whose interpretation is: he has heavy weight in good. And the meaning of ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ﴾ is: possessed of pleasure, with which whoever lives in it is pleased. Some said its meaning is "pleasing (marḍiyya)", and that comes back to this same meaning in the exegesis.

zajjaj:8-9.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأمّا مَن خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ﴾ ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ﴾ ("but as for him whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss"): that is, his dwelling is the Fire. His dwelling was called "his mother" because the root [of finding rest] is in taking refuge with mothers, so [the word] was substituted for what he takes refuge in: ﴿نارٌ حامِيَةٌ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 11] ("a blazing Fire").

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ ("and what will make you know what it is?"): the pausal form is ”هِيَهْ“, and the connected form is ”هِيَ نارٌ حامِيَةٌ“; but the hāʾ entered in pause to make clear the fatḥa of the yāʾ. What is obligatory is to follow the Muṣḥaf: one pauses on it and does not connect, and reads: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ ﴿نارٌ حامِيَةٌ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 11], because the Sunna is to follow the Muṣḥaf, and the hāʾ is written in it.
